original.target_description: Same-title 1999 primary conference paper located (ERIC ED437406), with hierarchical regression of global foreign language classroom anxiety on IAS, PAS, and OAS on manuscript pp. 12–13. Supplied locator is journal p. 99; published page not verified. Neutral locator does not identify which of the three predictor coefficients is the assigned effect.

replication.target_description: Hungarian secondary-school approximate replication; hierarchical/stepwise regression predicting FLCAS general language classroom anxiety from IAS, PAS and OAS. The individual predictor intended by this audit_id cannot be distinguished from the supplied neutral locator.

notes:
All three assigned IDs give the same study, general relationship description and page locators; none names an individual input/process/output predictor. Do not assign coefficients by input order. Original same-title conference manuscript is available, so original is locator_insufficient rather than paper_unavailable. It is a 1999 version with different author order; equivalence to the final 2000 journal p. 99 is unverified. The original omnibus regression p-value was not paired with an individual beta. Generic participant total was not treated as analytic n for an unidentified coefficient. Replication abstract is not full text and supplies no target statistics or narrative replication verdict. No completed target fields existed on entry. Locator-enriched revisit eligibility checked: the supplied original p. 99 and replication p. 63 are already recorded in this checkpoint. No additional page/table locator is supplied for the original locator_insufficient side; no side is eligible for re-extraction under the revisit restriction. Existing sides, statistic fields and author verdict are preserved; unchanged paper misses were not retried.
Source follow-up: Published book chapter version (2024); chapter PDF1–23 corresponds to printed49–71. Primary title verified against the supplied reference. Printed63 (chapter PDF15) was visually inspected. The broad supplied locator identifies a regression of FLCAS scores on IAS, PAS, and OAS, but neither the description nor study identifier nor page locator identifies which of these three predictors belongs to this audit_id. No predictor-to-audit_id mapping has been assumed from row order, duplicated descriptions, or numerical coincidence. Therefore the replication side is locator_insufficient and its statistic fields remain null. Independently located candidate results, retained here without row assignment: printed63, §4.5.3, paragraph below Table 4.7: “for input anxiety, β = 0.18, t = 2.42, p < 0.05; for process anxiety, β = 0.43, t = 5.32, p < 0.01; and for output anxiety, β = 0.31, t = 4.31, p < 0.01.” These are printed standardized-beta candidates with their same-test t and p bounds; none is assigned to this row. The model-level result (adjusted R² = 0.62; F₃,₁₂₉ = 73.90, p < 0.01) is a separate test and is not substituted for an individual predictor test. Printed53, §4.4.1, reports “Altogether 134 Hungarian high school students from four randomly selected schools in Budapest, Hungary took part in the study.” That is a recruited participant total, not an explicitly documented analytic n for the target regression; exclusions are not established, and analytic n has not been derived from degrees of freedom. Printed63 provides a narrative comparison: “These results suggest that anxiety experienced at the processing stage has a more significant effect on general language anxiety than anxiety experienced at the output stage of language learning, which is also consistent with Onwuegbuzie et al.’s (2000) findings.” This comparison is retained as evidence without assigning an individual-row reported-success verdict while the predictor mapping is unresolved.
